mainTopic: Cancelling a space by filling it (house versus ditch), planks over ditches and between balconies, and a haystack as a wall between two courtyards.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a contradiction. Our משנה says a ditch filled with dirt or pebbles is cancelled automatically, while the משנה in אהלות says a filled house is cancelled only if the owner actively cancels it. רב הונא says אהלות follows רבי יוסי, but a ברייתא shows רבי יוסי holds the opposite, so רב אסי says עירובין follows רבי יוסי instead. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that שבת and טומאה are different: for שבת, a person treats even a money-pouch as fixed for the day. רב אשי answers that a ditch is meant to be filled and a house is not. רבא then explains the משנה's lines about a plank over a ditch and a plank between balconies, using the rule of לבוד. A new משנה teaches that a haystack ten טפחים high is a wall between two courtyards. רב הונא forbids taking hay from it into a basket, and the גמרא defends him against a ברייתא about a house filled with hay. Finally, the גמרא tries to prove from that ברייתא that walls not reaching the ceiling still count. אביי rejects the proof, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע begins a second rejection that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the contradiction from אהלות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its inference from the משנה in אהלות: straw cancels the house only if the owner actively cancelled it. Otherwise it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he did not cancel it — no, it is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: This line ends a contradiction that began just before our passage. The משנה in אהלות says a house full of straw is cancelled 'if he cancelled it'. The גמרא now points out what follows from that: if he did not cancel it, the house is not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference 'if he did not cancel it, no' means that in אהלות, a house filled even with straw or pebbles (צרורות) is cancelled only if the owner actively cancels it. Our משנה in עירובין says a ditch filled with dirt or pebbles is cancelled automatically, with no act of cancelling, while straw never cancels the ditch. The clash is whether cancelling happens automatically or needs an active decision, and that is the contradiction the rest of this passage tries to solve.

keyTerms.meaning: He cancelled it, meaning he decided the material stays there permanently
Cancelled. The material becomes part of the space and the space loses its old status

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the last line of a contradiction that started on the previous amud: the משנה in עירובין about a ditch versus the משנה in אהלות about a house.

phrases.english: If he did not cancel it — no, it is not cancelled.
phrases.notes: An inference from the wording of the משנה in אהלות ('וביטלו').

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בִּיטְּלוֹ — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the contradiction that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה in עירובין, which treats a ditch filled with dirt or pebbles as cancelled automatically.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אהלות shows that filling a space cancels it only with an active act of cancelling ('ביטלו אין, לא ביטלו לא'). עירובין treats dirt or pebbles in a ditch as cancelled automatically.

steps.title: רב הונא: אהלות follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה in אהלות was taught by רבי יוסי. So the two משניות are written by different תנאים who disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Who taught אהלות? It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא solves the contradiction by saying the two משניות come from different תנאים. According to him, the משנה in אהלות is the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the simplest kind of answer: the two sources do not have to agree because different authors wrote them. On this view, the משנה in עירובין follows a תנא who does not accept רבי יוסי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught it? A question asking which תנא a source follows
מסכת אהלות, which deals with the טומאה of a dead body spreading under a roof

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Who is the tanna that taught Oholot?
It is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאן תָּנָא אֹהָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two sources to different תנאים who disagree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות follow one view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: אהלות follows רבי יוסי, and עירובין follows a תנא who disagrees with him.

steps.title: But רבי יוסי holds the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we know רבי יוסי holds the opposite of what רב הונא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי יוסי, we have heard the opposite from him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's answer by claiming that רבי יוסי's known view does not match the משנה in אהלות. This line sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'איפכא שמעינן ליה' means we have a tradition that רבי יוסי rules the other way. The actual source for this claim comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard him say, meaning we know his view

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yosei,
we have heard the opposite from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִיפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that אהלות follows רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's known view conflicts with the requirement in אהלות of active cancellation.

steps.title: The ברייתא: what matters is whether he plans to remove it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that for רבי יוסי everything depends on whether the owner plans to remove the material, not on what the material is.
steps.simpleTranslation: As was taught: רבי יוסי says, straw that he does not plan to remove is like ordinary dirt and is cancelled. Dirt that he plans to remove is like ordinary straw and is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing רבי יוסי's real view. For him, the type of material does not decide anything. The owner's plan to remove it or leave it is what counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the default depends on the material: ordinary dirt (סתם עפר) is cancelled automatically, with no act of cancelling, and ordinary straw (סתם תבן) is not. The owner's plan can override this default. This is the opposite of אהלות, which requires an active act of cancelling even for pebbles ('if he did not cancel it, no').

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
He plans to clear it out later
Ordinary or unspecified, meaning the normal case with no special plan

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets out the rule of רבי יוסי: the owner's plan, not the type of material, decides whether something is cancelled. The next answer depends on this rule.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Straw that he does not plan to remove —
it is like ordinary dirt, and it is cancelled.
Dirt that he plans to remove —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא כִּסְתַם תֶּבֶן, וְלֹא בָּטֵיל.
phrases.english: it is like ordinary straw, and it is not cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the challenge in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי does not fit the משנה in אהלות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי about straw and dirt with or without a plan to remove them.

steps.title: רב אסי: עירובין follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי flips the attribution: the משנה in עירובין is the one that follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אסי said: Who taught עירובין? It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: Since אהלות cannot be רבי יוסי, רב אסי gives a new answer. The משנה in עירובין is the one that follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the ברייתא: for רבי יוסי, ordinary straw is not cancelled, which is exactly what the משנה in עירובין says about the ditch. אהלות, which requires an act of cancelling, follows a תנא who disagrees with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous answer is dropped and a new one is offered
מסכת עירובין, our משנה about a ditch between courtyards

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Asi said:
Who is the tanna that taught Eruvin?
It is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: מַאן תְּנָא עֵירוּבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב הונא's answer, which the ברייתא disproved.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing which source is attributed to רבי יוסי
steps.terutzMaskana: עירובין follows רבי יוסי (ordinary straw is not cancelled), and אהלות follows a תנא who disagrees with him.

steps.title: טומאה and שבת cannot be compared
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says there is no contradiction, because טומאה and שבת follow different rules of cancelling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Are you setting טומאה against שבת? Leave aside the prohibition of שבת, since a person cancels even a money-pouch.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer rejects the contradiction itself. The laws of טומאה and the laws of שבת work differently, so their rules about straw do not have to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שבת, cancelling only needs to last for that day. A person treats even a money-pouch, which is מוקצה and will not be moved, as fixed in place. So dirt or pebbles filling a ditch are cancelled automatically, while straw, which may be moved on שבת, is not. For טומאה, cancelling must be permanent, so even pebbles in a house need a real act of cancelling.

keyTerms.meaning: You are raising a contradiction, setting one source against another

steps.whatToRemember: Approaches so far: (1) רב הונא says אהלות follows רבי יוסי, but the ברייתא rejects this. (2) רב אסי says עירובין follows רבי יוסי. (3) רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says there is no contradiction, because cancelling for שבת only needs to last that day, while cancelling for טומאה must be permanent and needs a real act of cancelling. רב אשי adds a fourth answer in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: The money-pouch line does not mean that cancelling for שבת is generally stricter. Even a valuable pouch counts as fixed on שבת, because it will not be moved that day. Straw is different only because it can be moved on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Are you raising a contradiction between impurity and Shabbat?!
Leave aside the prohibition of Shabbat,
for even a money-pouch too
a person cancels.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָה אַשַּׁבָּת קָרָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer that rejects the basis of the original contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two areas of law (שבת versus טומאה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rules about cancelling should be the same for טומאה and for שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: For שבת, material that will stay put that day (like dirt or pebbles) counts as cancelled automatically, though movable straw does not. For טומאה, cancelling must be permanent, so an explicit act of cancelling is needed.

steps.title: A ditch is meant to be filled, but a house is not
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says there is no contradiction, because you cannot compare a house to a ditch. A ditch normally stands to be filled. A house does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Are you really comparing a house to a ditch?! A ditch makes sense, since it is normally meant to be filled in. But is a house meant to be filled in?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another answer to the contradiction between our משנה (the ditch) and the משנה in אהלות (the house). He says the two cases are simply not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone puts dirt into a ditch, we assume it stays there for good, because ditches are usually meant to be filled. A house is meant to be lived in, so dirt or hay inside it is probably temporary and will be cleared out. That is why filling a house does not automatically cancel it, while filling a ditch does.

keyTerms.meaning: You are raising a contradiction (comparing two sources that seem to clash)
It makes sense with regard to… (sets up a contrast)
It stands to be filled in / sealed up

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer to the house-versus-ditch contradiction depends on what each place is normally used for. A ditch is meant to be filled, so filling it is permanent. A house is not, so filling it is assumed to be temporary.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Are you contrasting a house with a ditch?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. He means the two cases cannot be compared.

phrases.english: Granted, a ditch stands to be filled in.
But does a house stand to be filled in?
phrases.notes: Of course not. So filling a house is assumed to be temporary.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּיִת אַחָרִיץ קָא רָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a separate answer, next to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's answer in step 6, for the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (the two places have different normal uses)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought a house filled with dirt and a ditch filled with dirt should follow the same rule about cancelling.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ditch normally stands to be filled, so its filling is permanent. A house does not, so its filling is not assumed to be permanent.

steps.title: A plank placed along the length works even if it is narrow
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה's requirement of a plank four טפחים wide applies only when it is laid across the width of the ditch. If it is laid along the ditch's length, any width works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he placed on it a plank four handbreadths wide. רבא said: This was taught only when he laid it across the width. But if he laid it along the length, even a tiny plank works, because it shrinks the ditch to less than four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about putting a plank over the ditch, and רבא explains when that rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plank laid across the ditch works as a doorway, and a doorway must be four טפחים wide. A plank laid along the length does something else: it covers part of the opening, so the ditch is now less than four טפחים wide. A ditch that narrow no longer counts as a separating wall at all, so the plank's size does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of… (limits a rule)
Along its width (across the ditch) / along its length
Any amount at all, even tiny

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ways the plank works. Across the ditch, it is a doorway and needs four טפחים. Along the length, it narrows the ditch so the ditch is no longer a separation, and size does not matter.

phrases.english: If he placed on it a plank that is four handbreadths wide.
Rava said:
They taught this only where he placed it across its width,
but if along its length,
even any small amount also works,
since he has reduced it to less than four.
phrases.notes: The ditch is now narrower than four טפחים, so it no longer separates the courtyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּתַן לְרׇחְבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contradiction is now closed. The גמרא goes back to explaining the lines of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four-טפחים requirement applies only to a plank laid across the width. A plank laid along the length works at any width, because it narrows the ditch below four.

steps.title: Balconies must face each other directly
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the משנה's wording that a plank between balconies works only if they are directly opposite each other, not offset and not one higher than the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And similarly, two balconies opposite each other. רבא said: What you said, 'opposite each other,' means yes in that case. If they are not opposite each other, no. And if one is higher than the other, also no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about two balconies. רבא makes a precise inference from the words 'opposite each other.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically said 'opposite each other,' so רבא concludes that other arrangements do not work. If the balconies are offset sideways or one is higher, a plank between them is not a usable doorway, because walking across it would be awkward or dangerous. So the two courtyards cannot make one עירוב that way.

keyTerms.meaning: That which you said… (introduces a precise reading of a source)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ.
phrases.english: And similarly, two balconies opposite each other.
Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ — אִין,
phrases.english: That which you said, 'opposite each other': yes, it works,
if they are not opposite each other: no,
and if one is above the other, also no.
phrases.notes: The 'no' carries over from the previous phrase.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ — אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא continues explaining the משנה, moving to the next line, about balconies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plank between balconies counts as a doorway only when the balconies face each other directly. It does not work if they are offset or at different heights.

steps.title: A gap under three handbreadths makes it one bent balcony
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits his own rule. Offset or uneven balconies are a problem only if they are three טפחים or more apart. If the gap is smaller, they count as one bent balcony.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only when there are three handbreadths between this one and that one. But if there are not three between them, it is one crooked balcony.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the rule he just gave about balconies that are not opposite each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of לבוד, a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as if it were closed. So two balconies that are slightly offset or slightly uneven, with less than three טפחים between them, are seen as one balcony with a bend in it. In that case the plank still works.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in a case where… (narrows a rule)
Three handbreadths, the size limit for לָבוּד
The rule that a gap of less than three טְפָחִים counts as joined

steps.whatToRemember: Balconies that are offset or uneven do not work, unless the gap is under three טפחים. Then לבוד joins them into one bent balcony.

phrases.english: We said this only

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: where there are three handbreadths between this one and that one,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה —
phrases.english: but if there are not three between this one and that one,
it is one crooked balcony.
phrases.notes: Based on לבוד: a gap under three טפחים is treated as closed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This narrows רבא's ruling in step 9 to cases where the gap is three טפחים or more.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If balconies are offset or uneven by less than three טפחים, they count as one bent balcony, and the plank works.

steps.title: A haystack ten handbreadths high acts as a wall between courtyards
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. A haystack ten טפחים high between two courtyards is a separation, so each courtyard makes its own עירוב. If it drops below ten, they must make one shared עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A haystack between two courtyards that is ten handbreadths high: they make two עירובין, and they do not make one. These feed their animals from this side, and those feed from that side. If the hay shrank below ten handbreadths, they make one עירוב, and they do not make two.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a pile of hay can act as a wall between two courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten טפחים is the height of a halachic wall, so a haystack that tall separates the courtyards, and each one needs its own עירוב. Each side may feed its animals from the hay without worrying that the pile will shrink and stop being a wall. Once the hay is actually below ten טפחים, the wall is gone, and the two courtyards count as one area.

keyTerms.meaning: A haystack, a pile of straw

steps.confusionAlert: Feeding animals from the hay is allowed even though it may slowly shrink the wall. The status changes only once the hay is actually below ten טפחים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the main theme of the פרק: a partition made of usable material, like hay, still counts as a wall while it stands.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A haystack that is between two courtyards
and is ten handbreadths high:
they make two eiruvin, and they do not make one.

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ מַאֲכִילִין מִכָּאן, וְאֵלּוּ מַאֲכִילִין מִכָּאן.
phrases.english: These feed their animals from here, and those feed from there.
If the hay was reduced to less than ten handbreadths,
they make one eiruv, and they do not make two.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְבֵּן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It starts a new topic after the explanation of the ditch-and-balcony משנה is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A haystack ten טפחים high separates two courtyards, so they need two עירובין, and each side may feed from it. Once it is below ten, they need one shared עירוב.

steps.title: רב הונא limits how animals may be fed from the haystack
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the משנה's permission to feed animals from the haystack does not include taking hay into a basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא said: This is allowed only as long as the person does not put hay into his basket and feed his animal with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by adding a limit from רב הונא: the animals may eat from the haystack, but the owner may not scoop hay into a basket for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The haystack is what separates the two courtyards, so each side can make its own עירוב. If people take hay out by hand, the pile could drop below ten טפחים, and the separation would be gone. So רב הונא forbids taking hay by hand, as a protective rule.

keyTerms.meaning: provided that; only as long as

steps.whyThisMatters: This limit is what drives the rest of this passage. Both challenges that follow are aimed at it.

phrases.english: Gemara: Rav Huna said:
provided that he does not put [hay]
into his basket and feed [his animal].
phrases.notes: The worry is that removing hay by hand will shrink the pile below ten טפחים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתֵּן לְתוֹךְ קוּפָּתוֹ וְיַאֲכִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the feeding permission in the משנה from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals may eat from the dividing haystack, but the owner may not put hay into a basket and feed them, because that could lower the haystack below ten טפחים.

steps.title: Challenge: standing an animal next to the haystack should also be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how standing an animal by the hay can be allowed, given רב הונא's own rule from רבי חנינא that you may not stand an animal on מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it allowed to stand the animal there? But רב הונא said in the name of רבי חנינא: A person may stand his animal on grass on שבת, but a person may not stand his animal on מוקצה on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the animal may simply be placed next to the haystack. It uses another teaching that רב הונא himself reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With grass, the owner will be very careful not to pull any up for the animal, because pulling grass is a Torah-level איסור. With מוקצה, the איסור is only rabbinic, so the owner might grab some for the animal without thinking. Here, taking the hay is also only a rabbinic איסור, so standing the animal by the haystack should be forbidden for the same reason.

keyTerms.meaning: items set aside, which may not be handled on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that the more serious case (grass) is allowed and the lighter case (מוקצה) is forbidden. The reason is that people treat a Torah איסור seriously and will not slip up, but they may be careless with a rabbinic one.

phrases.english: And is it permitted to stand [the animal there]?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Huna say in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
A person may stand his animal
on grass on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: He will be careful, because pulling grass is a Torah prohibition.

phrases.english: But a person may not stand his animal
on set-aside items on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Since the prohibition is only rabbinic, he might move the items himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאוֹקֹמֵי שְׁרֵי? וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב הונא's limit from step 12, then argues that his reasoning should forbid even standing the animal next to the hay.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission (as limited by רב הונא) to bring animals to the haystack to eat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking the hay is a rabbinic איסור, just like מוקצה. Standing an animal on מוקצה is forbidden in case the owner handles it. So standing an animal by the haystack should be forbidden too.

steps.title: Answer: the owner only blocks the animal, and it eats on its own
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means the owner stands in front of the animal so it cannot wander off, and the animal walks over and eats by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he stands in front of the animal, and it goes and eats by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining the case in the משנה more narrowly. The owner does not lead the animal to the hay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about מוקצה forbids actively placing your animal on the forbidden items. Here, the owner only stands in the way so the animal does not stray. The animal goes to the hay on its own, so the worry does not apply.

phrases.english: Where he stands in front of it
and it goes and eats [on its own].

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָאֵים לַהּ בְּאַפַּהּ וְאָזְלָה וְאָכְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the owner brings his animal over and places it next to the haystack.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner only blocks the animal's path, and the animal eats by itself, so the מוקצה rule does not apply.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא that openly allows taking hay into a basket
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about a house filled with hay between two courtyards allows each side to put hay into a basket, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And may he not put hay into his basket? But a ברייתא teaches: A house between two courtyards that was filled with hay: they make two עירובין and not one. This one puts hay into his basket and feeds, and that one puts hay into his basket and feeds. If the hay dropped below ten טפחים, both are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's rule directly. A ברייתא openly allows each side to take hay into a basket. Steps 16-17 finish quoting the ברייתא, and step 18 answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's case, the hay is still the separation between the two courtyards, just like the haystack in the משנה. Yet it plainly allows each side to fill a basket and feed, which is exactly what רב הונא forbade. The ברייתא even mentions that the hay could fall below ten טפחים, and it still allows taking it.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the ברייתא itself admits the hay might fall below ten טפחים, which would forbid both sides. Even so, it allows taking hay into a basket. That is why it contradicts רב הונא so sharply.

phrases.english: And may he not put hay into his basket?
But it was taught: A house that is between two courtyards
and they filled it with hay:
They make two eruvin and do not make one eruv.
phrases.notes: The hay counts as a separation that divides the house.

phrases.english: This one puts [hay] into his basket and feeds,
and that one puts [hay] into his basket and feeds.
If the hay was reduced to less than ten handbreadths:
both are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יִתֵּן לְתוֹךְ קוּפָּתוֹ תֶּבֶן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב הונא's limit in step 12 and attacks it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule (step 12) that one may not put hay into a basket to feed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about hay that separates two courtyards openly allows each side to put hay into a basket and feed, even though the hay could fall below ten טפחים.

steps.title: The ברייתא explains how to fix the problem once the hay drops below ten
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If the hay sinks below ten טפחים and both courtyards become forbidden, one resident can lock his house and give up his rights in the area. Then he is forbidden to carry and his neighbor is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he act? He locks his house and gives up his rights. He is forbidden to carry, and his neighbor is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא it brought as a challenge to רב הונא. This line explains the fix once the hay is no longer a valid partition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the hay drops below ten, the two courtyards count as one area without a shared עירוב, so both are forbidden. One person can do ביטול רשות, giving up his rights, so that only one 'owner' is left and that person may carry. This line is part of the quoted source and is not yet the point of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He gives up his rights in the shared area (ביטול רשות)
How does he act? (asking for the practical solution)

phrases.english: How does he act?
He locks his house
and renounces his rights,
he is forbidden and his fellow is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד הוּא עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the ברייתא begun in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that hay may not be taken into a basket
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This line is part of the source being used against רב הונא. The actual attack comes in the next step.

steps.title: Same rule for a hay pit, and the גמרא pinpoints the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא applies the same rule to a hay pit between two תחומי שבת. The גמרא then points to the key line: each side puts hay into his basket and feeds his animal. This contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you say the same about a pit of hay between two תחומי שבת. In any case, the ברייתא teaches: this one puts hay into his basket and feeds, and that one puts hay into his basket and feeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a parallel case. Then the גמרא says 'קתני מיהת' to point at the exact words that challenge רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the משנה allows feeding only directly from the haystack, not taking hay into a basket. This ברייתא openly allows putting hay into a basket. So the contradiction is now stated clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: Shabbat boundaries (how far one may walk on שבת)
In any case, it teaches (pointing to the key line of a source)

phrases.english: And likewise you say
regarding a pit of hay
that is between two Shabbat boundaries.
In any case, it teaches:
this one puts into his basket and feeds,
and that one puts into his basket and feeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and turns it into a direct challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly allows putting hay into a basket, which is exactly what רב הונא forbade.

steps.title: A house is different because the drop in hay is noticeable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a house has walls and a ceiling, so when the hay goes down, people notice. With an open haystack, nobody notices, so רב הונא forbids taking with a basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: in a house, since there are walls and a ceiling, when the hay goes down, the matter is noticeable. Here it is not noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by showing the ברייתא is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking hay with a basket removes a lot quickly and can bring the pile below ten טפחים. In a roofed house the growing gap under the ceiling is obvious, so people will stop carrying in time. With the open haystack of our משנה the shrinking is not obvious, so רב הונא limits people to letting the animal eat directly.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא stands. Taking hay in a basket is allowed in a roofed house, where the drop is noticed, but not at an open haystack.

phrases.english: They say:
a house, since there are
(walls and) a ceiling,
when it decreases —
the matter is noticeable.
Here — the matter is not noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: בַּיִת, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (a house with a ceiling versus an open haystack)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's permission to use a basket applies everywhere, against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The basket is allowed only in a roofed house, where a drop below ten will be noticed. At the open haystack it is forbidden.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line about hay dropping below ten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to a line of the ברייתא: if the hay drops below ten טפחים, both courtyards are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the hay decreased to less than ten טפחים, both are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא re-quotes a line from the ברייתא to set up a new inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a repeat for nothing. The גמרא is going to read this line closely and draw a new rule from it in the next step.

phrases.english: If the hay was reduced
to less than ten handbreadths
both are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְמַעֵט הַתֶּבֶן מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב הונא discussion and returns to the ברייתא's wording for a new point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hay below ten טפחים is no longer a partition, so both courtyards are forbidden.

steps.title: Partitions that do not reach the ceiling still count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא implies that hay ten טפחים high is a valid partition even though the ceiling is far above it. So walls that do not reach the ceiling still count as walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that at ten it is permitted, even though the ceiling is much higher. Learn from this: partitions that do not reach the ceiling are considered partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a close reading of the ברייתא and proves a general rule about partitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only forbids when the hay drops below ten, so at ten it works. Yet the hay is inside a house and does not reach the ceiling, leaving a big gap. Since it still counts, a ten-טפח partition does not have to touch the ceiling.

keyTerms.meaning: But at ten it is permitted (an inference from the wording)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא tries to prove from the ברייתא that a ten-טפח wall counts even if it does not reach the ceiling. The next steps push this proof off.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether partitions that do not reach the ceiling count is debated elsewhere, and this ברייתא gives a proof that they do.

phrases.english: This implies at ten — it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמִידַּלְיָא תִּקְרָה טוּבָא.
phrases.english: even though the ceiling is raised much higher.
Learn from this:
partitions that do not reach the ceiling —
their name is partitions.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא עֲשָׂרָה שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the line quoted in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that partitions not reaching the ceiling count as partitions
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that the hay forbids only below ten, even though it sits in a house with a high ceiling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Proposed inference: ten-טפח partitions count even when there is a gap between them and the ceiling. This is rejected in steps 21-22.

steps.title: אביי: The house was just under thirteen handbreadths, so the hay is joined to the ceiling
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof by saying the ברייתא is about a house slightly less than thirteen טפחים high with hay ten טפחים high. The gap is under three טפחים, so לבוד treats the hay as reaching the ceiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Here we are dealing with a house that is slightly less than thirteen טפחים high, and the hay is ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is pushing back on the proof from Step 20. He says the ברייתא is not talking about a tall house where the hay is far from the ceiling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed there was a big gap between the hay and the ceiling. אביי says the house is just under thirteen טפחים and the hay is ten, so the gap is less than three טפחים. Because of לבוד, a gap under three טפחים counts as closed, so the hay counts as a wall reaching the ceiling, and the ברייתא proves nothing about walls that truly stop short.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (a specific case)
Missing a tiny bit; slightly less than
The rule that a gap of less than three טְפָחִים is treated as closed
A handbreadth, a unit of measurement

steps.confusionAlert: The word לבוד does not appear in the text. אביי's numbers only make sense because of לבוד: 13 minus 10 leaves a gap of just under 3, and under 3 counts as joined.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic way to reject a proof: narrow the case so the source no longer shows what it was brought to show.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Here, with a house of thirteen (handbreadths)
phrases.notes: Describes the height of the house in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: minus a tiny bit, we are dealing,
phrases.notes: Just under thirteen, so the gap stays under three טפחים.

phrases.english: and the hay is ten.
phrases.notes: Hay at ten plus a gap under three makes לבוד apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּבַיִת שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר חָסֵר מַשֶּׁהוּ עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 20 by limiting the case of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the hay ברייתא that walls not reaching the ceiling still count as walls.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a large gap between hay and ceiling. In the ברייתא's case the gap is under three טפחים, so לבוד joins the hay to the ceiling.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: Even in a house ten טפחים high
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע begins a second rejection of the proof. He says that even if the house is only ten טפחים high, the proof still does not work. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: You can even say the ברייתא is about a house ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא starts a different way to push off the proof. This line only sets up his answer, and the explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי needed a tall house, just under thirteen, so that לבוד would work. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says he does not need that. Even in a house exactly ten טפחים high, he will show that the ברייתא does not prove walls that stop short of the ceiling are valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say; you can even say (introduces a broader answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same person as the רב הונא whose ruling was discussed in Steps 12-18. This is רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, a different אמורא, the same one who answered in Step 6.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Even if you say with a house of ten
phrases.notes: Sets up his answer. The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּבֵית עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different rejection of the Step 20 proof. Unlike אביי, it does not require a tall house.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The same proof from Step 20, now rejected even if the house is only ten טפחים high.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated on this amud. The reasoning continues on the next amud.
